solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Observed to secure information back in web-savvy locations

indicators.note: back tells us the whole assembled string is read from right to left
to secure means the first word holds the second safely inside it

parts.note: observed means seen
a fact is a piece of information

explanation.surface: Someone was spotted guarding data at places where people know their way around the internet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' applies to the whole container built by 'to secure', not just to 'information', so the full eight letters are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Internet cafés are places where people go to get online, hence web-savvy venues.

clue.text: Clarifies the history of some mountains?

definitions.meaning: makes clear, sets out the reasons for
land that was once flat before being pushed up into ranges

explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as EX-PLAINS: 'ex' means former, and some mountain ranges were once flat land, so their past is 'former plains'. The question mark flags this playful geology.
explanation.definitionFit: To clarify something is to make it clear, which is what setting out the reasons does.

clue.text: Get rid of a length of waterway

parts.note: to can something is informal for to dismiss or scrap it

explanation.surface: An instruction to dispose of a stretch of a river or channel.
explanation.definitionFit: A canal is an artificial waterway dug for boats or irrigation.

clue.text: They'll have some more hopefully expecting a further delivery

definitions.text: They'll have some more hopefully expecting a further delivery

parts.words: They'll have some more hopefully expecting a further delivery
parts.note: reads like customers awaiting another parcel, but the 'delivery' is a birth and 'expecting' is pregnancy, which these medicines help bring about

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests shoppers waiting for another order. 'Expecting' means pregnant and 'delivery' means giving birth: the clue describes medication taken by people hoping to conceive.
explanation.definitionFit: Such medicines help would-be parents conceive, so those taking them hope to be expecting and later give birth.

clue.text: Traduced composer's story conveyed in a variety of airs

indicators.note: conveyed in means the story is carried inside the other letters
a variety of signals that the letters of the next word appear in a different order

parts.note: a story can be a lie, as in 'telling stories'

explanation.surface: A slandered musician's tale is passed on through a range of melodies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Traduced' is fair: the composer was rumoured, without evidence, to have poisoned Mozart, a story dramatised in the play and film Amadeus. 'a variety of' and 'conveyed in' are the indicators.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonio Salieri was the Italian composer slandered by the legend that he murdered his rival Mozart.

clue.text: Divinity only half apparent in spring festival

indicators.note: only half apparent says just the front half of the synonym can be seen

parts.note: divinity, the quality of being godly, is holiness

explanation.surface: A god only partly shows himself during a festival held in spring.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLINESS has eight letters; 'only half apparent' keeps its first four.
explanation.definitionFit: Holi is the Hindu festival of colours, celebrated at the start of spring.

clue.text: This really sees length cut before arrangement?

definitions.text: This really sees length cut before arrangement?

indicators.note: arrangement signals that the remaining letters are set out in a new order
cut means the following letter is snipped out of the phrase

explanation.surface: A trip to the hairdresser: hair is trimmed shorter and then styled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' removes one L from THIS REALLY, leaving THISREALY, and 'arrangement' rearranges those nine letters. The whole clue also describes a haircut followed by styling.
explanation.definitionFit: A coiffure is made by trimming hair and then arranging it, which the clue describes.

clue.text: Supporter took in ambassador

parts.note: a leg supports a table or chair
took in food means ate

explanation.surface: A backer who accepted a diplomat, or swallowed his story.
explanation.definitionFit: A legate is an envoy, especially one representing the Pope, so an ambassador.

clue.text: Modern art style is out for use in coating front of palace, possibly

indicators.note: for use means the contraction is put to work inside the jumbled letters
possibly signals that the letters could be arranged another way
front of picks out the first letter of the word

parts.note: ain't is a colloquial contraction of 'is not', with out read as not

explanation.surface: A new kind of art is no longer used for painting the façade of a royal residence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges IN COATING plus P (the 'front of' palace) to ACTIONPING, and 'for use' slots AINT ('is out', i.e. is not) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Action painting is the mid-20th-century abstract style of Jackson Pollock, with paint dripped or flung on canvas.

clue.text: First in work? Begin, losing little time

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a musical work

indicators.note: losing tells us a letter is dropped from the synonym

parts.note: to enter is to begin, as in entering a contest
T is the short form of time

explanation.surface: A query about who starts a job, then an instruction to start without delay.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is 'First in', the cricket batsman who goes in first, not 'First'.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the opening batsmen are the first players in to bat for their side.

clue.text: Workshy, though not initially deficient

indicators.note: not initially means the synonym loses its opening letter

parts.note: someone workshy is slacking

explanation.surface: A lazy worker who, oddly, isn't short of anything at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking means wanting or short of something, the same as deficient.

clue.text: Smoother excellent line feed in river

indicators.note: in places the first pieces inside the river

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river
A1 means first-rate; crosswords render it AI
LF is the computing abbreviation for line feed

explanation.surface: A first-class food for fish floats down a river to make things smoother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smoother' is a noun here, a thing that smooths, not the comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A file for the fingernails is used to smooth rough edges, so it is a smoothing tool.

clue.text: Smallish creatures not caught in smallish pictures

indicators.note: not says a letter is to be left out

parts.note: insects are small creatures
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Little animals don't appear in miniature illustrations.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a small picture or map set within a larger one.

clue.text: Negligence in Spain, with plenty refusing American backing

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: refusing means the plenty word turns away some of its letters

parts.note: a sufficiency is plenty, enough

indicators.note: backing means those letters are read in reverse

explanation.surface: Carelessness in Spain, with abundance rejecting American support.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns US into SU, and 'refusing' removes those letters from the start of SUFFICIENCY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of efficiency and care amounts to negligence, a failure to perform well.

clue.text: Leaders of finance identify record implicating University College regarding trust funds

indicators.note: leaders of takes the opening letters of the next words
implicating means the record wraps around the college

parts.note: a diary is a daily record
UC is the abbreviation for University College

explanation.surface: Finance chiefs find a document incriminating a college over its investments.
explanation.definitionFit: Fiduciary describes holding money or property in trust on someone else's behalf.

clue.text: Decay entering stone is most disturbing

indicators.note: entering means the decay goes inside the stone

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for stone, the weight
caries is tooth decay

explanation.surface: Rot seeping into masonry is the most alarming sight.
explanation.walkthrough: A stone is a British weight of 14 pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Scariest is the superlative of frightening, so most disturbing.

clue.text: Resort period: ocean bathe almost entirely free

parts.note: a day is a period of time

indicators.note: free signals the letters are loosed into a new order
almost entirely means the phrase loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A holiday spot: for a while you can swim in the sea at no charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost entirely' drops the final E of OCEAN BATHE, and 'free' rearranges OCEANBATH to TONABEACH.
explanation.definitionFit: Daytona Beach is a Florida seaside resort famed for its motor racing.

clue.text: Most suitable reduced period in work reduced minutes

indicators.note: in puts the shortened period inside the shortened work
the second reduced cuts the last letter from the work word

parts.note: an opus is a work, especially of music

indicators.note: reduced means the period word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: time is a period

explanation.surface: Mechanical-sounding instructions for trimming a schedule down to the ideal.
explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'reduced' is a deliberate echo: each one trims its own neighbouring synonym by its last letter, and 'in' joins the two trimmed pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimum means the best or most favourable, hence most suitable.

clue.text: Spiced meat is served up after a flight's boarded

indicators.note: boarded means the escape is taken on board inside the turned word
served up, in a down clue, reads the word from bottom to top

parts.note: on the lam means in flight, on the run

explanation.surface: A cured sausage is dished up after an aeroplane has been boarded: in-flight catering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' suits a down entry, where reading upwards turns a word round; 'boarded' then takes the flight phrase on board. 'On the lam' is American slang for on the run.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured sausage seasoned with garlic and spices.

clue.text: Note a mark of injury in autosport

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by a wound

explanation.surface: Remark on the wounds that motor racing leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: NASCAR is the American stock-car racing organisation, and by extension the sport itself.

clue.text: Metal treatment involving tritium, just a little

parts.note: tin is a metal

indicators.note: involving means the treatment wraps round the element symbol

parts.note: a cure is a medical treatment
T is the chemical symbol for tritium

explanation.surface: Processing metal with a small dose of tritium.
explanation.definitionFit: A tincture can mean a slight trace or tinge of something, so just a little.

clue.text: Month in Jerusalem? Part of August is right

indicators.note: Part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a certain month in Jerusalem coincides with August.
explanation.definitionFit: Tishri, also spelt Tisri, is the first month of the Jewish civil year, falling around September and October.

clue.text: Live outside Spanish resort, disdaining American mix

indicators.note: outside means the verb goes round the resort

parts.note: I am means I live or exist, giving AM

indicators.note: disdaining means the resort spurns one letter

parts.note: Malaga is a resort on Spain's Costa del Sol

explanation.surface: Staying out of a Spanish holiday town, avoiding the American crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend or combination, so a mix.

clue.text: Publisher is a person at court?

parts.note: someone who sues takes a case to court

explanation.surface: Is the publisher a courtier? the clue seems to ask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a person at court' suggests a courtier, but it means a litigant.
explanation.definitionFit: One who issues, or puts out, books or banknotes is a publisher of them.

clue.text: Frothy, made from milk, taking day

indicators.note: taking means taking away, so the abbreviation is removed

parts.note: dairy products are made from milk

explanation.surface: A light, foamy drink made with milk, prepared in a day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something airy is light and insubstantial, like froth.

clue.text: Artist friend filled with determination

indicators.note: filled with means the friend is stuffed with the determination

parts.note: a mate is a friend
grit is determination

explanation.surface: A painter's companion is full of resolve.
explanation.definitionFit: René Magritte was the Belgian surrealist painter.
